reasoning: Step 1: Selected TL-IN-76101000 as the best match for 'aluminium window frames' based on description alone.
Step 2: The chosen line is not excluded and has CEPA status PREFERENTIAL, so preferential treatment is available.
Step 3: MFN rate is 10% (tariff and effective) and the 2026 CEPA rate is 0%.
Step 4: Origin rule PSR-IN-R118 'CTSH + VA 45%' applies; all checks pass, so origin QUALIFIES.
Step 5: Duty saving is ESTIMATED at 10000.00 AED based on the shipment value.
Step 6: Procedure steps assembled from the agreement, ministry service pages and the certificate fee tool.
Step 7: Caveats recorded from tool notes and passages that affect interpretation.

classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: All checks passed: final manufacture in UAE, minimal operations exceeded, CTSH satisfied (all 3 non-originating inputs classified outside subheading 761010), VA build-down 49.0% against threshold 45% on FOB basis. Totals: 6 inputs, 3 non-originating (51% of price).

procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism. The factory must be outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added; registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Fill in the application form, upload proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice and (for a trading exporter) the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online: AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000 (fee range AED 10–200).
Submit the application; processing takes about one working day and the service runs 24/7. Approval is received, or a return with comments to correct.

Print the approved certificate. It must be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export; a retrospective issue is possible up to 12 months from shipment with 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.
The certificate is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import.
Provide the certificate to the Indian importer, who claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years.
The exporter must keep origin records (including cost breakdown) for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

Goods must be shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. Third-party invoicing is allowed if the exporter indicates it.

caveats.note: India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value, so actual duty amounts will differ from the estimate based on the shipment value given.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 via LiveLaw, taxmann), not confirmed in the official text.
The agreement says box 8 for remarks, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year record-keeping minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The agreement does not define 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' used in the build-up method.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
